ideas: What you believed before reading it
The argument or story that changed your view
How you think or act differently now

phrases.meaning: slowly start to accept an idea

model: The book I'd like to talk about is Why We Sleep by Matthew Walker, a neuroscientist at the University of California, Berkeley. I read it about three years ago, when I was working really long hours and often sleeping only five hours a night. Back then, I took sleep for granted. I tended to see it as wasted time, and I was actually quite proud of getting by on so little. A colleague lent me the book, and to be honest I expected it to be boring, but it turned out to be a real page-turner. It opened my eyes to how much sleep affects memory, mood and even the immune system. Everything is backed up by research, although a few of his claims are arguably a bit exaggerated, according to some scientists. Even so, it seems to me that the main message is right, and it definitely changed my perspective. At first I didn't want to believe it, but gradually I came round to the idea that sleep is basically a performance tool. So I started to put it into practice. I stopped checking my phone in bed and set a regular bedtime of eleven o'clock. I'd say I'm noticeably more focused at work now, and I get ill far less often. It gave me a lot of food for thought, and I've recommended it to quite a few friends since.
